summary:
Planet X & SPHEREx Epoch Explorer is an interactive public sky-survey web portal designed to empower citizen scientists and astronomers to explore data from NASA’s SPHEREx and AllWISE missions.
​To address the challenge of detecting faint, elusive celestial objects—such as the brown dwarf WISE 0855—among massive datasets, we developed a full-stack application powered by FastAPI and specialized astronomical libraries (Astropy, Astroquery). Our pipeline processes multi-epoch FITS imagery, performs World Coordinate System (WCS) alignment, and applies FFT-based Difference Imaging to strip away static background stars, isolating moving objects and transient phenomena across detectors (D1–D6). It also cross-matches candidates against Gaia DR3 and AllWISE catalogs with built-in offline caching for uninterrupted reliability.
​This tool matters because it democratizes complex astrophysical analysis, transforming raw infrared survey data into an accessible, reproducible visual experience that accelerates the discovery of hidden solar system neighbors and variable cosmic targets.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works
Planet X & SPHEREx Epoch Explorer is an interactive web portal designed to analyze multi-epoch infrared sky-survey imagery from NASA’s SPHEREx and AllWISE missions. Users input astronomical coordinates—such as the brown dwarf WISE 0855 (RA: 133.795129°, Dec: -7.245147°)—or select celestial targets to retrieve and visualize raw FITS cutouts across different detectors (D1–D6) and time epochs.
Our processing pipeline performs World Coordinate System (WCS) alignment and applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) phase-correlation Difference Imaging. By subtracting static reference templates from new observational epochs, the system strips away stationary background stars and noise, isolating moving objects, high-proper-motion stars, and transient phenomena. Finally, an automated Catalog Cross-Match engine queries Gaia DR3 and AllWISE to verify whether a detected moving feature is a previously cataloged object or a new, unrecorded candidate.
​2. Benefits & Expected Impact
Astronomical FITS files and multi-catalog cross-matching usually require specialized desktop software and steep technical expertise. Our platform lowers this barrier, empowering citizen scientists, students, and researchers to visually hunt for elusive solar system neighbors (like Planet Nine candidates or cold brown dwarfs) directly from any web browser. By making epoch-by-epoch comparison intuitive and shareable via dynamic URL state synchronization, it accelerates collaborative discovery and scientific verification.
​3. Tools, Languages & Technologies Used
​Backend & Scientific Processing: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Astropy (FITS parsing & WCS alignment), Astroquery & PyVO (IRSA/TAP archive queries), NumPy/SciPy (FFT Difference Imaging & PSF false-positive filtering).
​Frontend & Visualization: React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and custom FITS-to-PNG rendering pipelines with interactive timeline playback, detector switching (D1–D6), contrast scaling, and Field-of-View (FOV) controls.
​Database & Deployment: SQLite (with serverless /tmp fallback) for search history logging, local JSON/FITS caching, and full-stack cloud deployment on Vercel.
​4. Creativity & Innovation
​Interactive Difference Imaging Toggle: Users can seamlessly switch between original FITS renders and processed Difference Imaging frames in real time, turning complex astrophysical subtraction into an intuitive visual "blink comparator."
​Reproducible Science via URL State Sync: Every parameter (RA, Dec, FOV, detector, bandpass) dynamically binds to the browser URL, allowing researchers to share an exact discovery view with a single link.
​Multilingual & Accessible Coordinate Parsing: Built-in Unicode normalization allows users to enter coordinates seamlessly in both English and Arabic numerals without encoding errors, paired with clear, human-friendly status alerts.
​5. Key Factors Considered by Our Team
​Offline-First Resilience: External astronomical servers (IRSA, VizieR, Gaia) frequently experience downtime or 502/503 latency under heavy load. We engineered a protected local JSON/FITS caching system (Offline Fallback) so core targets like WISE 0855 load instantaneously even without internet access.
​False-Positive Mitigation: To prevent sensor artifacts or cosmic rays from masquerading as discoveries, we integrated variance maps, data quality flags, and Point Spread Function (PSF) checks.
​User Experience & Simplicity: We replaced raw technical backend errors with clear, plain-language feedback explaining what each detector and catalog match means for the user.

Development Constraints & Context:
During this intense 48-hour hackathon, our team faced unique logistical hurdles, including an abrupt shift from an in-person venue to a virtual format with unstable internet connectivity, forcing us to migrate online mid-session entirely without on-site technical mentors. Despite these obstacles and the tight 48-hour window, our collective persistence enabled us to deliver a robust, offline-first solution.
